problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>1$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=5,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{5s-4}{{s}^{2}-s},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-4}{{s}^{2}-s}-5 \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-4}{s(s-1)}-5 \\  & =\frac{5s-4}{s-1}-5 \\  & =\frac{1}{s-1}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$
